abstract: Corona on wires is discussed in relation to the recent determination of ionization and attachment co-efficients in air. articleTitle: The economic generation of high-energy discharges
publicationTitle: Transactions of the South African Institute of Electrical Engineers
abstract: The production of high-energy capacitor discharges is considered chiefly from the point of view of efficiency. Two well-known circuits employing respectively a resistor and a low-resistance choke in the charging circuit of the discharge capacitor are analysed and their efficiencies discussed. In the case of one, its efficiency is shown to be theoretically bounded to below 50 per cent. Four new circuits are introduced which employ an electrolytic reservoir-capacitor in the charging circuit and no inductance. With all of these efficiencies exceeding 80 per cent can readily be achieved. The four circuits are further compared and it is shown that some offer certain advantages over others. A design procedure for the circuits is given. The operation of a pulser into an inductive load is discussed.

abstract: What is meant by guidance and control? Guidance is the art of generating the necessary information to direct an object to a predetermined target. Control is the technique by which the object is kept responsive to guidance commands. A guidance system consists of sensors, to determine the location of the object and its motion at any time, and a computer, to calculate appropriate commands to the control system so that the object will arrive at the target. A control system consists of control surfaces and propulsion devices which can change the velocity and direction of the object, and power amplifiers and actuators which can translate the guidance commands into suitable actions.
